security_audit.summary: Most command-related static findings are false positives from markdown references or JavaScript template literals, not shell execution. The skill does include legitimate outbound error telemetry, user context capture, and live error streaming examples that require privacy and access-control safeguards. No prompt injection text was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Outbound error telemetry may include user or runtime context.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit allowlists for user fields, request metadata, stack extras, cookies, and headers before events leave the application.

remediation.issue: The monitoring endpoint and API key are configurable in examples.
remediation.suggestion: Require trusted HTTPS endpoints, secure secret storage, rotation guidance, and a warning against hardcoded credentials.

remediation.issue: The live error stream example does not show access-control requirements.
remediation.suggestion: Document authentication, authorization, rate limiting, and redaction requirements for any dashboard error stream.

content.value_statement: Production errors are hard to triage when logging, alerts, and grouping are inconsistent. This skill guides structured monitoring, error routing, dashboards, and recovery workflows.
actual_capabilities: Assess existing error handling, logging usage, monitoring coverage, and common failure patterns.
Design Sentry-style error capture with filtering, sampling, context enrichment, and grouping.
Plan structured logging with production transports, audit events, and performance timers.
Define alert channels, escalation rules, severity levels, and noise-reduction thresholds.
Outline dashboards for error rate, affected users, MTTR, trends, and live streams.
Recommend recovery patterns such as retries, circuit breakers, and graceful degradation.
limitations: It cannot validate vendor credentials, service quotas, or account-specific feature limits.
It needs project context and runtime details to produce accurate implementation guidance.
Generated monitoring code must be tested before production deployment.
It cannot guarantee compliance without a separate privacy and retention review.

use_cases.title: Roll out production monitoring
use_cases.description: Create an error tracking plan with alerts, ownership, grouping rules, and dashboard metrics for a production service.

use_cases.title: Add structured debugging signals
use_cases.description: Improve application logs, error context, tracing, and recovery paths during a reliability upgrade.

use_cases.title: Reduce alert noise
use_cases.description: Review existing alerts and define severity thresholds, routing rules, deduplication, and escalation policies.

prompt_templates.title: Audit my error tracking
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of current monitoring coverage.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my service for error tracking gaps. Check logging, exception capture, alerts, grouping, and dashboards. Give prioritized recommendations.

prompt_templates.title: Design alerting workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate setup for triage and ownership.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an alerting workflow for this application. Include severity levels, routing, escalation, deduplication, and test cases for signal quality.

prompt_templates.title: Plan privacy-safe telemetry
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced implementation with sensitive data controls.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a privacy-safe error telemetry plan. Include redaction rules, user context limits, retention guidance, and checks before sending data to vendors.

prompt_templates.title: Build a reliability rollout plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced rollout across services and teams.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a phased rollout plan for error monitoring across multiple services. Include instrumentation, dashboards, alert tuning, ownership, and production validation.

output_examples.input: Review a Node service before production launch.
output: Finding: unhandled promise rejections are not captured by the current monitoring path.
Recommendation: add a global handler, send sanitized errors, and define a fatal shutdown policy.
Validation: trigger a controlled rejection in staging and confirm alert routing and dashboard visibility.

output_examples.input: Create alerts for a customer-facing checkout service.
output: Critical alert: sustained checkout error rate above the agreed threshold for five minutes.
Warning alert: repeated payment provider timeouts with automatic grouping by provider and region.
Noise control: suppress known validation errors and review alert volume after the first release week.

output_examples.input: Improve error dashboards for an incident review.
output: Dashboard additions: error rate, affected users, top error groups, deployment markers, and MTTR trend.
Triage view: recent errors grouped by service, owner, severity, release, and first-seen time.
Follow-up: add links from each dashboard panel to logs, traces, and runbooks.

best_practices: Start with data classification and redaction rules before adding new telemetry fields.
Validate alerts with controlled test errors in staging before production release.
Tune sampling, grouping, and escalation rules after real incident reviews.
anti_patterns: Sending full requests, cookies, headers, tokens, or personal data to monitoring tools.
Alerting on every error without ownership, severity rules, or deduplication.
Deploying monitoring changes without staging tests, rollback steps, or alert-volume checks.

faq.question: What does this skill help implement?
faq.answer: It helps design error tracking, structured logging, alerts, dashboards, grouping, and recovery workflows.

faq.question: Does it support Sentry-style monitoring?
faq.answer: Yes. The playbook includes patterns for Sentry-style capture, filtering, sampling, and context enrichment.

faq.question: Can it reduce noisy alerts?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides severity levels, routing, deduplication, thresholds, and validation with test errors.

faq.question: Can it inspect my production system directly?
faq.answer: No. It needs the user or agent to provide project context, permissions, and runtime details.

faq.question: How should sensitive data be handled?
faq.answer: Use allowlists, redaction, limited user context, secure credentials, and retention rules before sending telemetry.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
